scope: Bounded external sequential runner controls only. No Docker call, native build, actual container cleanup or installed acceptance.

findings.title: Cleanup stopped a reusable name after inspecting an owned identity
findings.reproduction: An inert Docker adapter returned an owned immutable ID; the actual cleanup function then issued docker stop against its mutable name. Replacement between inspection and stop could target another container.
findings.fix: Use the per-run CID file when available, validate exact image/session/immutable ID, stop only the inspected64-hex ID and reinspect only that ID. Exact NotFound is absence; permission, daemon, timeout and malformed results remain errors.
findings.retest: Name-reuse, foreign identity, NotFound and unknown inspection controls pass without stopping a foreign target.

findings.title: SIGTERM bypassed cleanup and failure recording
findings.reproduction: An actual owned scratch Python runner with inert process adapters received SIGTERM after entering a fake build: exit-15, durable status still running, cleanup never invoked.
findings.fix: SIGTERM raises a handled failure, repeated TERM is ignored during bounded cleanup, and previous signal handling is restored afterward. Failure state is written atomically with file/directory fsync when storage permits.
findings.retest: Actual scratch runner and inert child receive SIGTERM; original error propagates, exact-ID cleanup facade is invoked and the inert child is gone. This is not real Docker cleanup proof.

findings.title: Failure or identity journaling errors could prevent cleanup
findings.reproduction: Actual run_sequence with real scratch files and inert process adapters: inject ENOSPC only when writing stopped-on-failure. The exception escaped before stop_owned_container was called. Identity journaling had the same ordering dependency.
findings.fix: Failure and cleanup identity journaling are best-effort. Persistence errors are retained in memory/reported where possible and cannot prevent verified exact-ID cleanup or replace the original build/termination error.
findings.retest: Original scratch reproduction now invokes cleanup once and preserves the original CalledProcessError. Eleven controls also cover transient/persistent ENOSPC during actual inert SIGTERM plus foreign/absent/unknown inspection safety under failing journals.

independentChecks.limits: Real scratch files/locks, real SIGTERM and inert Python children; synthetic Docker facade, no actual container. Expected injected journal/inspection errors appear in test output.

independentChecks.check: Independent reproduction retake: persistent failure-journal ENOSPC with original build exception
independentChecks.result: cleanup invoked once; original exception identity preserved

independentChecks.check: Independent existing-log and actual advisory-flock conflict controls
independentChecks.result: prior log bytes preserved; no process launch when either guard rejects

independentChecks.check: Explicit GO argument and superseded-source hold
independentChecks.result: controls reject before acquiring the shared production lock or starting work

inputAndResourceReview.preQtPreparationChecks: Both proof copies and all27 input hashes matched. Three pinned-image plans preserve FreeAI2→Voice39→Connect6 order, CPU2, RAM4GiB, RAM-plus-swap6GiB and MAKEFLAGS=-j2; runtime/Connect sources are read-only mounts. Actual image inspection was not run by this reviewer.

Root must commit/repin the accepted Qt source/archive/manifests, refresh copied contexts and both proof hashes, update runner pins, and obtain the bounded independent identity retake before clearing the hold.
inputAndResourceReview.coordinatorAuthority: An empty workload inventory, advisory lock or successful control test is not admission. Root owns GO after reconciling the active Craft ISO slot; no dependency on finishing the entire Craft program is introduced.

limitations: SIGKILL, machine failure and total runner loss cannot run cleanup. Reconcile only exact recorded CID/image/session evidence; never stop by mutable name or broad process/container patterns.
Persistent ENOSPC can leave stale durable running state even after cleanup. The report and tests do not claim a failure receipt can be persisted onto a failing filesystem.
Actual Docker ownership/cleanup behavior, immutable builder image identities and resource enforcement remain untested by this no-Docker review.
Runner build completion means acceptance-pending. Owning tests, archive/ABI/capsule/dependency/notice/overlap and native/live checks remain separately required.
operations: Reviewer edited only this report for the runner review. No runner/source modification, shared lock acquisition, Docker/VM operation, native build, host install, credential access or provider request.
